note: UTE G1 per-family retirement ledger (revised 2026-11-20 after the external review). The four terms are the owner's predicate (RetireAllowed = OldBaseline AND NewPathVerified AND SemanticDifferencesResolved AND NegativeControlsPass). Three rules the gate enforces and this ledger cannot talk its way out of: (1) `unit.familyId` is resolved against dev/agent-workflow/ledgers/arc-a-family-census.json, so a row cannot shrink the retirement unit to the tools it happened to verify; (2) coverage is derived from the baseline TSV's `entry` column and the new path's `NEW-PATH-VECTOR <id>` lines, so a member with no vector is refused rather than absorbed; (3) every declared `oldPath.files` entry is checked for presence, and scripts/eb3-family-definitions.mjs turns required CI red (DEF_RETIREMENT_UNLICENSED) if one is deleted while the row is not allowed. `state` remains a mirror of the computed verdict. See docs/plans/memo/ute-g1-20261120/RETIREMENT.md.

negativeControlsPass.note: Four family-level controls (NC-1 lane bites, NC-2 harness bites on a mutated golden cell, NC-3 no legacy fallback, NC-4 the lane is load-bearing) PLUS one real control per retirement-unit member on the legacy path: NC-MEMBER read (widen only the read lane -> the refusal becomes a leak), NC-MEMBER write (widen only the write lane -> the file appears), NC-MEMBER edit (drop only the edit version guard -> a stale edit applies), NC-MEMBER read_image (widen only the image read lane -> an out-of-lane image read materialises a 70-byte attachment). Each NC-MEMBER is paired with NC-MEMBER-POSITIVE proving the unmodified run still reproduces its golden row, so no control is vacuous. A green FS control is not evidence for Web or PTY.

differences.summary: A `grep` call WITHOUT `path` returns ZERO matches on the product route: the host module omits the path operand from argv and the confined child's fd 0 is a readable socket, so ripgrep searches stdin instead of the session workspace (the tool description says a missing path defaults to the workspace). The governed row always appends `.` and returns the real set. MEASURED both ways on one fixture (SD-PATHLESS in semantic-differences.txt) and recorded as the product behaviour in golden row SR-G2-no-path-stdin. APPROVAL: PENDING (owner signature required) — this is a measured defect, not a reinterpretation.

The two implementations select DIFFERENT file sets for the same pattern: the route-C confined face runs ripgrep with `--no-ignore-parent --no-ignore-vcs` (a VCS-ignored file IS searched), while the governed row adds `--no-ignore-parent --no-ignore-global` only (VCS ignore stays in force, so the same file is NOT searched). MEASURED: the observed route-C argv (read from the confined provider call record) vs `searchArgv()` from packages/tools/search-family/src/search-backend.mjs, both executed on one fixture; only-route-c = the .gitignore'd file. APPROVAL: PENDING (owner signature required).

A withheld search surfaces differently: on route C every confined denial produces the SAME model-facing text ('subprocess failed before reporting an outcome (ripgrep provider failure)') and the cause exists only as the realm's a5sf-guard-consult/1 fact (IO_READ_DENIED — the same code for a lane denial and a missing target), while the governed row owns a closed per-cause SEARCH_REFUSAL_TEXT vocabulary and no guard-fact channel. Both map onto the same closed category here, but a consumer keying on the model-facing error cannot distinguish the cases on route C. APPROVAL: PENDING (owner signature required).

semanticDifferencesResolved.note: All three differences are retirement-blocking=YES and none has an approval record, so this term is FALSE today by construction, not by opinion. They were MEASURED, not asserted: probe-semantic-differences.mjs runs the governed lane's own exported argv builder and the argv the confined provider ACTUALLY received against the same fixture and compares the selected sets. Declared in tests/ute-g1-search/lib/semantic-differences.mjs, printed on every probe run, and asserted UNRESOLVED by lane-suite.test.mjs. The old-path fixture maps all refusals onto the same closed vocabulary the FS unit uses, so the differences do not block the BASELINE — they block RETIREMENT. All three were RE-MEASURED after merging origin/master 19a7fa641 (#802) and are unchanged (post-merge-remeasurement.txt §3): they are properties of the host search module and the confined argv law, not of the FS continuation #802 repaired — measured, not inferred.

negativeControlsPass.note: Two family-level controls (NC-HARNESS-BITES: a flipped golden match digest must go RED; NC-CATEGORY-TOTAL: an unexplained refusal must raise REFUSAL_VOCABULARY_INCOMPLETE and `unknown` must be unreachable) PLUS one REAL control per retirement-unit member: NC-MEMBER grep (widen ONLY the read lane -> the refused out-of-lane grep succeeds and returns the planted secret) and NC-MEMBER glob (the same widening -> the refused walk lists the out-of-lane path). Each is paired with NC-MEMBER-POSITIVE proving the unmodified vector still reproduces its golden row, so no control is vacuous. Two composition controls prove the routing is the authority: NC-SHADOW-LOAD-BEARING (dispose the realm's own PD-16 search shadow -> the out-of-lane grep leaks) and NC-STDIN-LOAD-BEARING (the same disposal turns SR-G2's path-less zero into real matches). The lane suite re-runs the whole transcript and refuses a verdict line that is not GREEN with failed=0. A green SEARCH control is not evidence for FS, Web or PTY. RE-RUN on the merged tree (origin/master 19a7fa641): still NC-VERDICT GREEN controls=8 failed=0.
